scope: Concrete video degradation triage; no production thresholds changed in this cycle.
problem_statement: Good audio can coexist with unnecessary video quality reductions. Video stability and recovery are the current priority.
The 200ms end-to-end synthetic audio test is a recorded diagnostic, not the current optimization target. It differs from the 200ms current-buffer guard and the 200ms local video work deadline.

The shared six-sample growth detector can still reduce video for a brief low absolute buffer rise: source0 63/63/77/99/99/109ms produced a second bad sample and a two-rung cut at128s; the next sample fell to99ms.
Fresh repeated concealment also caused a two-rung cut at176s. Do not attribute all reductions to the 200ms ceiling.
Raw cumulative video loss includes padding and temporary gaps. These need separate analysis from permanent image payload loss.

next_acceptance_criteria: Replay the recorded brief buffer rise and require video to hold its acknowledged quality while the buffer drains.
Tune growth magnitude and persistence separately from a sustained-buffer safety ceiling; tolerate short spikes, preserve reaction to actual interruptions and persistent overload.
Qualify recovery by decoded image counter, resolution and sampled freezes; retain raw audio measurements without making200ms the release blocker for this investigation.
Change one guard at a time and compare identical recorded policy input before another full media capture.
